Often, but not always. The results show examples where bundles cost less: a BLUETTI AC180 with a 100W panel is listed at **$649**, versus **$748** for the parts separately—a **$99 saving** ([PowerSized](https://powersized.com/solar-generator-kits/)). But some bundles cost the same as their components, and a sale on the station or a cheaper compatible third-party panel can make buying separately less expensive ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/solar-generator-kit-vs-buying-separately)).

Compare the bundle price with the *current* prices of the exact station and panel, and check that any separate panel’s voltage and connector are compatible. Bundles are also simpler: one purchase and often unified support.

judge.why: The only concrete example, a BLUETTI AC180 with a 100W panel at $649 versus $748, comes from PowerSized. That isn't our 200 W kit, and Dealectric is cited only for the general caveat.
